title: Pick a domain where an LLM being correct actually helps, and prefer culture over code
summary: A sphere earns its keep when an incoming LLM would otherwise be wrong or slow in a niche and recurring area: money-accounting discipline, containment around live models, Python or bash best practice, a vintage platform. Within a genuinely large system, the higher-value product is often not more code but its engineering culture and its hard-won conventions, because that is exactly what a fresh model cannot infer from reading source.
evidence_note: The bashqueues build found that the valuable sph- extract was the codebase's engineering culture (grounded via docs/*_CONTRACT.md and the bin/ idioms) rather than anything bashqueues had not already written. The money sphere encoded Accounting Core's knife-edge precision and filing invariants rather than re-listing its classes.
invariants: Choose domains that are recurring AND where correctness requires local knowledge a model cannot memorise from corpora.
In a large maintained system, extracting its conventions and doctrine is usually more valuable than adding feature code.
Do not re-encode what the source already speaks clearly; encode the hard parts and the seams.
One narrow, deeply-grounded sphere beats one broad, shallow one.
